solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Begins losing heart to boxer's attacks with words …

indicators.note: the middle letter of the first word is lost and the fighter's word takes its place

parts.note: begins means opens, as a show opens
a pug is slang for a pugilist, a boxer

explanation.surface: A fighter who starts out losing courage hits back with words instead of fists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart to' swaps the central E of OPENS for PUG. The definition carries on into the next clue: this one attacks with words, 5 Across 'or with teeth'.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppugn is a formal verb for disputing or calling into question, a verbal assault.

clue.text: The best part is stopping crude address to old lady

indicators.note: the abbreviation plugs the gap in the call, like a stopper

parts.note: oi is a rude way of hailing someone
mum is one's mother, the old lady in slang; to joins it on

explanation.surface: The best bit is when someone halts a rude remark aimed at an elderly woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude address' is the rude British shout 'oi!', and 'old lady' is slang for one's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The optimum is the most favourable or ideal outcome, the peak of quality.

clue.text: Dig around Jungfrau's base not level with surface

indicators.note: the poke goes around the single letter

parts.note: a dig is a prod or poke

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Excavating around the foot of the Jungfrau, a peak in the Swiss Alps, where the ground is uneven.
explanation.definitionFit: A surface feature that stands proud projects slightly above what surrounds it.

clue.text: Change of regal concerns is admitted by top-level authoriser

indicators.note: the worries are let into the rearranged royal letters
a change of the word means its letters are reordered

parts.note: what concerns you is what eats you, as in what's eating you

explanation.surface: A regime change whose worries are admitted by the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: GREAL, the anagram from 'Change of regal', takes in EATS after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The seal applied to state documents in Britain to authorise them in the monarch's name.

clue.text: In America this court visitor would be ineffectual

indicators.note: the answer goes in the abbreviation for America to make the word for ineffectual, so taking it away leaves the answer

parts.note: ineffectual means useless

explanation.surface: An American who suggests a visitor to the court would be useless there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' asks for the answer placed inside the abbreviation for America to give the word for ineffectual. Monica Seles was a tennis champion of the 1990s, a visitor to tennis courts.
explanation.definitionFit: A tennis star is a visitor to courts, and Seles was one of the most famous players of her era.

clue.text: … or with teeth (see answer accepted by pundits)

indicators.note: the pundits take in the other letters, holding them within

parts.note: pundits are wise men, sages
V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Continuing the attack theme: a reply welcomed by the experts, read as a bracketed aside.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this to 1 Across: 'attacks with words … or with teeth', so the definition here borrows 'attacks' from the clue before.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that savages someone attacks them by biting, the toothed counterpart of verbal assault.

clue.text: Drawing lots of mosaic-piece graphics primarily, and touchy about it

indicators.note: the sensitive word goes about, around, the other pieces

parts.note: touchy means sore, sensitive
a mosaic is made of tiles

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the word's opening letter

explanation.surface: A touchy artist sketching lots of mosaic tiles with graphics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing lots' looks like sketching many pictures; it means casting lots to tell the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Sortilege is divination by casting or drawing lots, an old form of fortune-telling.

clue.text: Maybe frequent verb marks the end?

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for verb in grammar
this is it is said when something is finished

explanation.surface: A grammar note on whether a common verb ends a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frequent' looks like an adjective describing the verb; it is the verb meaning to go often to a place.
explanation.definitionFit: To frequent a place is to go there often, an example of calling on it.

clue.text: Ignite and lay about for warmth

indicators.note: about here means round about, rearranged

explanation.surface: Lighting a fire and lying around it for warmth.
explanation.definitionFit: Geniality is friendly warmth of manner, cheerful kindness.

clue.text: Expert did a slalom, perhaps crossing lines

indicators.note: the skier's word goes across, around, the letters for lines

parts.note: a slalom is a ski race, so whoever did one skied
L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: An expert skier weaving through slalom gates, crossing the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Expert and skilled both describe someone highly practised and able.

clue.text: I may put plaster on torso with separate internal cuts apparently more healed?

indicators.note: two separate letters from inside the body word are cut away, leaving its ends and one middle letter

parts.note: someone more healed is, jokingly, more well; apparently flags the made-up comparative

explanation.surface: A patient with a plastered torso and stitched cuts seems to be getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: Cutting the first O and the S out of TORSO leaves TRO, the only way to make two separate internal cuts. WELLER is a whimsical comparative of well.
explanation.definitionFit: A plasterer applies plaster with a trowel, so a trowel-wielder is one who puts plaster on walls.

clue.text: Involving university, regressively bars religious group

indicators.note: the turned-round pubs wrap around the single letter for the college
going backwards, so the word for bars is read from its end

parts.note: bars are pubs, inns

explanation.surface: A university that bans a religious group, going backwards in its policy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunnis form the larger of the two main branches of Islam.

clue.text: Spray that has daisy's head in the centre

indicators.note: the fine spray holds the flower's first letter within it

parts.note: a fine spray of water droplets is a mist

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A garden sprinkler wetting the flower at the middle of the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: In the midst of something means in its middle, so the noun names the central part.

clue.text: Christian convert to depict his old identity with an exchange of origins?

indicators.note: the two words swap their opening letters, origins being beginnings

parts.note: to depict in art is to paint
Saul was the name of the apostle before his conversion on the road to Damascus

explanation.surface: Asking a convert to portray the person he used to be before his conversion.
explanation.walkthrough: PAINT SAUL becomes the answer once the P and S at the starts of the two words change places.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle to the Gentiles was converted to Christianity after a vision on the Damascus road.

clue.text: French port, according to locals seen in wellies rampaging about

indicators.note: about turns the letters round, so they are read backwards
the letters can be seen running inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A French port where the locals spot people in wellington boots running riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'wellies rampaging' backwards and the port sits in it, from the M of 'rampaging' to the E of 'wellies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French city of Marseilles is spelt without the final S by its own inhabitants.

clue.text: Retired cops still considered handling differently

indicators.note: to cop is to catch or hold, so the abbreviation holds the other word

parts.note: still, in the sense of nevertheless, is though

explanation.surface: Retired police officers still mulling over a case they handled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cops' looks like police officers; it is a verb meaning catches or holds, the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Reconsidering means reviewing an approach to arrive at a new one.

clue.text: I'll put on a plastic coat to beat wearing a short blue one

definitions.text: I'll put on a plastic coat

parts.note: to lam is to beat or thrash
in means wearing, as in dressed in

indicators.note: short means the word is cut off before its end

parts.note: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so a blue one is a Tory

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to protect a short Tory in a plastic coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A laminating machine seals paper inside a clear plastic layer.

clue.text: Issue was disheartening after pulling article from Elle

indicators.note: once the article is pulled out, what remains of the first word is left

parts.note: something that chilled you was disheartening, sending a shiver
le is a French definite article, fitting a French magazine

explanation.surface: A magazine issue was depressing after a piece was pulled from Elle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a magazine number beside Elle; it is the definition. The French article LE comes out of CHILLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the sense of offspring, a son or daughter, as in dying without issue.

clue.text: Are these weapons to show path for warning shot?

definitions.text: Are these weapons to show path for warning shot?

parts.words: Are these weapons to show path for warning shot?
parts.note: split in two words, the answer says where a warning shot at sea is fired, across a ship's front

explanation.walkthrough: A warning shot is fired across the bows of a ship. The weapons themselves fire bolts.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons that shoot bolts from a bow mounted crosswise on a stock.

clue.text: Come to after 'little one' is a large!

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A child coming round and asking for a large drink.
explanation.definitionFit: When a bill comes to a sum, that sum is its sum total; the verb means add up to.

clue.text: Showpiece for key players rounding duck and double century with bye

indicators.note: the farewell goes around the cricket letters

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal goodbye
a duck, a score of nothing in cricket, is O

indicators.note: double asks for the letter for a hundred to appear twice over

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A cricketing tale of a duck, a double century and a bye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bye' looks like the cricket extra run; it is a farewell. 'duck' is a cricket score of nothing, shaped like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A toccata is a virtuoso keyboard piece designed to display the player's touch.

clue.text: Muses bearer, 'What to make of men's money?'

indicators.note: the question invites us to make something new from the letters

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about what to do with some men's cash.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titaness of memory bore Zeus the nine Muses.

clue.text: Seemingly one without a lisp, dropping a sibilant, but he tries

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is let fall from the coined word

parts.note: someone who can say the letter S, an ess-sayer, apparently has no lisp
S is a sibilant, a hissing sound

explanation.surface: A person who tries hard to speak without lisping drops a hissing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: Seemingly flags the coined word ESS-SAYER; dropping one of its three S's gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayer is one who essays, makes an attempt.

clue.text: Tight wardrobe covering back tattoos

indicators.note: the cupboard wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard or wardrobe

indicators.note: back means the word for tattoos is read in reverse

parts.note: to ink someone is to tattoo them

explanation.surface: A tight garment from the wardrobe hiding the tattoos on someone's back.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-knit group is tightly bonded, like closely woven fabric.

clue.text: MDMA powder taken up for impressive effect

parts.note: MDMA is ecstasy, E in slang

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: talc is a fine powder

explanation.surface: Drugs and powder snorted up for a dramatic effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliance of success or display, conspicuous flair.

clue.text: Closed? That's awful unlucky

parts.note: a door pulled to is closed
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Finding a shop shut and grumbling about bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough luck means bad luck, so the adjective describes misfortune.

clue.text: Expressions of despair in sound volume

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the word for volume is heard as the answer

parts.note: volume means size, how big something is

explanation.surface: Groans of despair coming loudly through the speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Long audible breaths let out in sadness or weariness are signs of hopelessness.

clue.text: Guts in age should reveal morbid person

indicators.note: the guts of each word are its insides, the letters without its ends

explanation.surface: Bravery in old age should expose a person obsessed with death.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghoul is someone with an unhealthy interest in death and the macabre.

clue.text: Language for computing run that breaks everything

indicators.note: the short word goes into the larger one, breaking it open

parts.note: everything means all
to run, as an engine does, is to go

explanation.surface: A program run that crashes the whole system.
explanation.definitionFit: An early high-level programming language from 1958, its name short for Algorithmic Language.

clue.text: Repetition unknown, having tightened up old journal earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the three pieces ahead of the unknown in the answer

parts.note: rope that is tightened up is taut
a log is a journal or record
Y is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: An unknown writer having tightened up an old diary from an earlier time.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless saying of the same thing twice in different words, as in free gift.

clue.text: Like familiar pharaoh, ruler showing more perception

parts.note: like means as, in comparisons
Tut is the familiar short name for the pharaoh Tutankhamun
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A ruler as shrewd as the famous boy pharaoh.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewder, sharper-minded, quicker to see what is really going on.

clue.text: Luther's reformed cheat

indicators.note: reformed means changed in form, so the letters are reshaped; a nod to Luther and the Reformation

explanation.surface: The church reformer Martin Luther branded a cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A con artist or swindler who gets money by deception.
